title: Orchestration vs. Workflow Automation vs. Case Management: A Taxonomy for Financial Services
summary: Orchestration, workflow automation, and case management are not synonyms. This taxonomy names the difference, maps each class to FS use cases, and gives a decision guide before you buy.
body_markdown:
### Summary


- **Three distinct categories.** Durable execution (Temporal, AWS Step Functions, Conductor OSS), BPMN workflow automation (Camunda 8), and case management (Pega, Appian, ServiceNow) solve different problems, yet vendors market them interchangeably.
- Category mismatch is expensive. Choosing from the wrong class shows up as months-long implementations, rising integration costs, and administrator headcount rather than as an obvious product defect.
- Classify the use case before evaluating vendors. Payments and data pipelines belong in durable execution, fixed audit-heavy approvals belong in BPMN, and fraud, disputes, and claims belong in case management.
- Durable execution is a technical guarantee that most workflow labels do not confer. Most "workflow engines" do not persist state after every step, and error-handling code typically makes up more than two-thirds of production systems.
- **One platform can span all three.**[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) builds and deploys deterministic, on-prem workflows across the orchestration and BPMN classes at 15–60x lower run cost than fully stochastic agents.


Financial services buyers evaluating automation platforms face a terminology problem before they face a technology problem. Vendors apply the words "orchestration," "workflow," and "case management" interchangeably in sales materials, and the market has largely accepted that conflation. The result is costly: teams select tools from the wrong category and then spend months discovering the mismatch.


The confusion is significant enough that generative AI systems also misclassify it. Asked to recommend a workflow orchestration tool, a language model may suggest Confluent, a streaming data platform, or conflate Netflix Conductor with a business process management suite. These are separate categories governed by separate design principles.


This article defines three distinct classes of automation tooling relevant to financial services, maps each to its appropriate use cases, and provides a decision guide for buyers who need to choose correctly the first time.


---


## Class 1: Durable Execution and Workflow Orchestration


Durable execution is the most technically precise of the three classes, and the most frequently mislabelled.


[Temporal defines durable execution](https://temporal.io/blog/what-is-durable-execution) as crash-proof execution: code that continues running correctly despite process crashes, machine failures, and software bugs. The execution engine persists state at every step, so when a failure occurs, work resumes from the last checkpoint rather than from the beginning. The error-handling code that typically constitutes more than two-thirds of production systems becomes unnecessary.


Most tools marketed as "workflow engines" do not provide this guarantee. The distinction matters at scale and in regulated environments where a failed payment or interrupted data pipeline carries financial and compliance consequences.


The core technical disciplines of this class are:


- Durable state: Execution state is persisted to a store after every step. A process restart replays the recorded history and continues forward.
- Determinism: Workflow logic must produce the same output for the same input. All side-effecting calls, including API requests, database reads, and LLM queries, are isolated into discrete activities and are never called directly from the workflow definition.
- **The Saga pattern:** The[saga orchestration pattern](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/saga-orchestration.html) uses a central orchestrator to manage distributed transactions across multiple services. If any step fails, the orchestrator triggers compensating transactions to roll back prior steps. Saga participants must be idempotent: retries must not double-apply an effect such as debiting an account twice.


**Representative tools:**[Temporal](https://temporal.io/solutions/financial-services) , AWS Step Functions,[Netflix Conductor](https://github.com/netflix/conductor) (now continued as Conductor OSS via Orkes; the original Netflix repository was archived December 2023). For data-oriented workloads, Dagster, Airflow, and Prefect occupy a variant of this class focused on pipeline scheduling and observability.


**Financial services use cases:** Payment flows, transaction processing, provisioning workflows, and data pipelines.[Temporal's financial services customers](https://temporal.io/solutions/financial-services) include Coinbase, Checkout.com, Remitly, Macquarie, Brex, ANZ, Intuit, and Kotak, all running mission-critical transactional workflows on durable execution infrastructure.


---


## Class 2: BPMN Workflow Automation


Where durable execution is an execution guarantee, BPMN workflow automation is a modelling discipline.


Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) is an international standard for representing business processes as visual diagrams. A BPMN-based tool converts those diagrams into executable process definitions: a fixed, auditable sequence of tasks, gateways, and events that runs the same way every time. The primary concern is capturing the business logic correctly and making it inspectable by both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


The canonical tool in this class is Camunda 8. Camunda 8 is specifically relevant because its[Zeebe execution engine](https://www.zenml.io/blog/temporal-alternatives) incorporates durable execution properties, placing it at the intersection of Class 1 and Class 2. Camunda spans both the modelling discipline of BPMN and the execution guarantees of the durable execution class.


**Financial services use cases:** Loan origination, new account opening, standardised compliance checks, and multi-level approval flows. These processes share a common profile: they involve a defined sequence, require a full audit trail of who acted at each step and when, and must execute consistently across every instance.


The distinction from Class 1 is the starting point. Durable execution starts with reliability: the question is how to guarantee that a distributed transaction completes. BPMN workflow automation starts with the process model: the question is how to represent an approvals sequence accurately so that it is auditable and governable.


---


## Class 3: Case Management


Case management handles work that cannot be fully specified in advance.


[Camunda's case management documentation](https://camunda.com/solutions/case-management/) defines this category as coordinating long-running, complex processes that weave people, systems, and dynamic tasks that evolve as new information arrives, priorities shift, and exceptions appear. A fraud investigation does not follow the same path every time. A complex insurance claim may require evidence that was not anticipated when the case was opened. A regulatory disclosure may trigger sub-processes that alter the original timeline.


The structural characteristic of case management is the combination of a deterministic backbone with ad-hoc flexibility. Repeatable sub-processes, such as identity verification or a standard compliance check, run as structured BPMN flows within the case. But knowledge workers retain the authority to add tasks, reroute work, bring in specialists, and respond to information that the original process definition could not anticipate.


This is the category experiencing the most direct impact from agentic AI. AI agents can now perform the judgment-heavy work that previously required a knowledge worker for every interaction: interpreting unstructured documents, cross-referencing prior cases, drafting responses to regulatory queries. What keeps these agents governable is the case management layer that surrounds them, with its role-based access controls, audit logs, and escalation paths.


**Representative tools:** Pega, Appian, and ServiceNow dominate the established market. Camunda 8 also addresses this class through its support for human task orchestration alongside BPMN process definitions.


**Financial services use cases:** Dispute resolution, insurance claims processing, fraud investigations, complex customer onboarding, and regulatory disclosures. Financial institutions including[Jyske Bank](https://camunda.com/solutions/case-management/) use case management platforms to handle the structured-but-flexible character of these workflows.


## Which Class Do You Actually Need? A Decision Guide for Financial Services


The three classes address three different primary problems. Mapping a use case to the right class before evaluating vendors eliminates the most common source of failed evaluations.


**Use durable execution (Class 1) when:**


- The process spans multiple services or systems and must complete atomically, even across failures
- A partial failure has a financial or compliance consequence (double-charge, unreconciled ledger entry, dropped transaction)
- The workflow runtime is measured in seconds to minutes but must be fault-tolerant from the first step
- The organization is building or operating data pipelines where each step must be observable and recoverable


*Tools to evaluate:* Temporal, AWS Step Functions, Netflix Conductor / Conductor OSS, Dagster


**Use BPMN workflow automation (Class 2) when:**


- The process sequence is fixed and well-understood before build begins
- Auditability of the sequence itself is a regulatory requirement, not just auditability of outcomes
- Business analysts and compliance officers need to read and validate the process model directly
- The goal is standardizing an approval or review sequence that currently runs inconsistently across teams


*Tools to evaluate:* Camunda 8


**Use case management (Class 3) when:**


- The process cannot be fully specified in advance because outcomes depend on evidence gathered during execution
- Knowledge workers need the authority to add tasks, change routing, or escalate outside the standard path
- Human judgment is required at certain decision points regardless of automation maturity
- The same nominal process (e.g., "fraud investigation") produces materially different execution paths across instances


*Tools to evaluate:* Pega, Appian, ServiceNow, Camunda 8


One additional signal: when vendor evaluation conversations focus on integration cost, implementation duration, and administrator headcount rather than the technical design of the process, the tool category may already be wrong. Platforms that fit the problem reduce those concerns. Implementation timelines measured in months, licensing as a starting cost, and post-purchase hiring around a platform are indicators of category mismatch as often as they are indicators of a poor product choice.


---


## The Spanning Layer: Jinba


The three-class taxonomy describes the problem space, and a single platform can address more than one class.


Jinba is a YC-backed, SOC II compliant platform that spans the workflow-orchestration layer and operates as a developer platform and tooling ecosystem purpose-built for large regulated enterprises in banking and insurance. Its product line addresses each class in the taxonomy while sharing a unified governance and deployment foundation.


**Jinba Flow covers Class 1 and Class 2.**


Flow builds, tests, and deploys reusable enterprise workflows through chat-to-flow generation or a visual editor. Workflows publish as APIs, batch processes, or MCP servers. The execution model is 80% deterministic: rule-based steps run without invoking an AI model, which brings the operational cost to $5–20 per month at scale compared to $300 or more for fully stochastic agent-based execution, a cost difference of 15 to 60 times.


Flow includes human-in-the-loop approval steps natively. A` WAIT_FOR_APPROVAL` step pauses a run until a human approves or rejects via an in-chat approval card or the run console. The step is implemented as a first-class workflow card. For processes that require documented human sign-off at a defined point, this closes the gap between automation and compliance requirement.


For regulated environments, Flow supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment, private model hosting on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, or self-hosted infrastructure, RBAC, SSO, audit logging, version control, feature flags, and over 100 integrations. These are the properties that address the legacy integration wall and the administrator burden that make category-wrong platforms so expensive in practice.


**Jinba App Neo covers Class 3.**


App Neo is the Claude-native agent layer: governed, shared Claude agents designed for team use. Agents connect to published Jinba Flow workflows through the` jinba-flow` connector, a call-only integration that exposes any published workflow as a callable tool. An agent handling a complex customer dispute can execute a deterministic compliance check flow, pause for a human approval, then continue, all within a single governed session.


App Neo supports scheduled tasks, persistent memory across conversations, role-based access with Owner and Member roles, and native MCP server connections. Each agent run is captured as a reviewable chat thread, which provides the audit trail that case management in financial services requires.


**Jinba Brain is the knowledge layer that sits above all three classes.**


Brain is a knowledge layer, not a retrieval-augmented generation system or a vector database. It stores company-specific knowledge as ontology-validated, schema-validated, linked records, making data answerable rather than merely findable. Where a general-purpose data layer such as Snowflake makes data accessible, Brain makes it consistent: every AI agent answers from the same verified facts rather than generating a fresh inference from raw documents on each query.


For financial services specifically, Brain ships with FIBO (the EDM Council Financial Industry Business Ontology) for banking and the ACORD Information Model for insurance as its base Layer 1 schemas. Every record carries a source path and SHA-256 hash for full traceability. Knowledge updates in both learning loops, one driven by new data and one driven by user interaction, require human review before going live. There are no automatic knowledge updates.


**Jinba Toolbox** is the developer-facing component: a centralized tool registry and execution platform for AI agents, self-described as npm for AI tools. Toolbox integrates with Flow, allowing workflows to call tools registered in a Toolbox organization, and supports any MCP server via a custom connector.


---


## What to Do Next


The three classes are distinct, and the cost of selecting the wrong one accumulates over the full implementation lifecycle, not just at licensing.


For financial services teams currently evaluating platforms, the first question is which class the actual use case belongs to. Payment processing and data pipelines belong in Class 1. Fixed approval sequences with compliance audit requirements belong in Class 2. Dispute resolution, claims handling, and fraud investigation belong in Class 3.


Teams that need all three, or that need to move between them as their automation programme matures, should assess whether a platform built to span the workflow-orchestration layer from the start is more efficient than assembling three separate point solutions and managing their integration overhead across regulated infrastructure.


---


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the difference between workflow orchestration, BPMN workflow automation, and case management?


Workflow orchestration (durable execution) guarantees a distributed transaction completes reliably, BPMN workflow automation models a fixed and auditable approval sequence, and case management coordinates unpredictable, evidence-driven work. These are three separate tool categories, not interchangeable features. Durable execution tools like Temporal focus on crash-proof reliability; BPMN tools like Camunda 8 focus on visual, business-readable process definitions; case management platforms like Pega and Appian handle work that cannot be fully specified in advance.


### Is case management the same as BPM?


No. BPM (Business Process Management) and BPMN model a fixed, repeatable sequence that runs the same way every time. Case management coordinates work that changes based on information discovered during execution, giving knowledge workers the authority to add tasks, reroute work, and escalate. Many case management platforms include a BPMN backbone for repeatable sub-processes, but the case layer adds the ad-hoc flexibility BPM alone cannot provide.


### When should a bank choose Temporal instead of Camunda?


Choose Temporal when the priority is guaranteeing that a distributed transaction completes reliably across failures, such as payment processing and data pipelines. Choose Camunda when the priority is a visually modeled, auditable approval sequence that business analysts and compliance officers can read directly. Camunda 8's Zeebe engine incorporates durable execution, so it can serve both needs; Temporal remains the more specialized choice for pure execution reliability.


### What is durable execution and why does it matter for payments?


Durable execution is crash-proof code execution: the engine persists state at every step so that after a failure, work resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from the beginning. For payments, this prevents partial failures with financial and compliance consequences, such as double-charging an account or dropping a transaction. It also eliminates most of the error-handling code that typically makes up more than two-thirds of production systems.


### What is the Saga pattern and why do financial workflows need it?


The Saga pattern uses a central orchestrator to manage distributed transactions across multiple services. If any step fails, the orchestrator triggers compensating transactions to roll back prior steps. Financial workflows need it because a failed multi-step transaction, such as a payment that debits one account but fails to credit another, must be reversed cleanly. Saga participants must be idempotent so that retries never double-apply an effect like debiting an account twice.


### Why do AI tools recommend the wrong workflow orchestration software?


Because vendors and the market use "orchestration," "workflow," and "case management" interchangeably, generative AI trained on that conflated language recommends tools from the wrong category, for example suggesting Confluent (a streaming data platform) or conflating Netflix Conductor with a business process management suite. The solution is to classify the use case first, then evaluate vendors inside the correct category.


### Can AI agents handle regulated financial workflows?


Yes, when they run inside a governed case management layer. AI agents can interpret unstructured documents, cross-reference prior cases, and draft responses to regulatory queries, but what keeps them governable is the surrounding case layer with role-based access controls, audit logs, and escalation paths. For additional safety, mix deterministic rule-based steps with AI so that compliance-critical logic never depends on stochastic model output.


### What is the difference between Netflix Conductor and a BPM suite?


Netflix Conductor is a durable execution workflow engine (now continued as Conductor OSS via Orkes) for orchestrating microservices and distributed tasks. A BPM suite such as Camunda provides visual BPMN modelling, business-analyst-readable process definitions, and auditability of the sequence itself. Conductor focuses on execution reliability; BPM suites focus on modelling and governance of the process.


### How do you choose a workflow automation platform for compliance-heavy processes?


Start by classifying the use case before looking at any vendor: fixed payment and pipeline flows belong in durable execution, fixed audit-heavy approval sequences belong in BPMN automation, and evidence-driven work like fraud investigation belongs in case management. Then check for on-premise deployment, RBAC, SSO, audit logging, and domain framework support such as FIBO and ACORD. If vendor conversations focus on integration cost, implementation duration, and administrator headcount, the category is likely wrong.


### How much does it cost to run AI-powered workflow automation?


Cost depends heavily on how much of the workflow relies on AI models. Fully stochastic agent-based execution can cost $300 or more per month at scale, whereas an 80% deterministic execution model, where rule-based steps run without invoking a model, brings operational cost to $5 to $20 per month, a difference of 15 to 60 times. For regulated, high-volume workflows, deterministic-first design is typically the cheaper and more compliant approach.
